pr_title: Improve index uid validation upon API key creation
pr_body:
- ~Use an IndexUid newtype to enforce stronger constraints~
- ~`cargo update -p vergen`~ (`rustup update` was the proper fix for this)
- Add a new `meilisearch_types` crate
- Move `meilisearch_error` to `meilisearch_types::error`
- Move `meilisearch_lib::index_resolver::IndexUid` to `meilisearch_types::index_uid`
- Add a new `InvalidIndexUid` error in `meilisearch_types::index_uid`
- Move `meilisearch_http::routes::StarOr` to `meilisearch_types::star_or`
- Use the `IndexUid` and `StarOr` in `meilisearch_auth::Key`

Fixes #2158

issue_context.title: API key creation should returns an error
issue_context.body: **Describe the bug** While creating an API key we can specify the indexes it applies to. And if we specify a [bad formatted index name](https://github.com/meilisearch/specifications/blob/main/text/0061-error-format-and-definitions.md#invalid_index_uid) we’re supposed to get an [`invalid_api_key_indexes`](https://github.com/meilisearch/specifications/blob/develop/text/0061-error-format-and-definitions.md#invalid_api_key_indexes) error from what I see. That’s not the case. The same happens for the update route. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Send the following request: `echo '{ "actions": [], "description": "test_error_create_key", "indexes": ["invalid index # / \\name with spaces"], "expiresAt": null }' | http :7700/keys 'Authorization: Bearer masterKey'` 2. Get the result: ``` { "actions": [], "createdAt": "2022-02-09T14:47:49Z", "description": "test_error_create_key", "expiresAt": null, "indexes": [ "invalid index # / \name with spaces" ], "key": "AG5o4s740edcfd04ce86f2a92259ca6f886485caf22ebb156b91211ac4e10119482f6e67", "updatedAt": "2022-02-09T14:47:49Z" } ``` **Expected behavior** Error **Screenshots** **Meilisearch version:** v0.25.2 **Additional context** I gave you my private key please don’t hack me. --- Edit by @curquiza TODO: The spec specifies: > Sending a value that is not a valid `index` (e.g. regarding the index uid format) in the `indexes` field returns an [invalid_index_uid](0061-error-format-and-definitions.md#invalid_index_uid) error. See https://github.com/meilisearch/specifications/pull/112/files We want to make the search engine returns an error when the index uid is invalid Definitely something that can be fixed by an external contributor! Feel free to ask for help
comments: I had a similar discussion with @gmourier about the error one should get when `GET`ing an index with a badly formatted index uid, I was on the side of returning a badly formatted index name error here, before the index doesn't exist error, but he was aging the opposite. Anyway, the result is that we return an  index not found error. So what you get seems consistent with that to me

Huuum but the error I'm expecting is in the spec though.
And in my case I don't get *any* error.
What do you think @gmourier ?

Thanks, I understand the problem better!

Indeed, we could add a variant of the error message in this case. It can be also extended to the `actions` field that works in the same way (expecting valid values). Currently, we just check that it is an array made of string. Thus, we already have a [message](https://github.com/meilisearch/specifications/blob/main/text/0061-error-format-and-definitions.md#invalid_index_uid) for it. (See message field).

Nevertheless, I make the difference between filling a value for an API resource model (this specific case) and requesting a resource via `GET`.

It makes sense to me to get a 404 when the resource doesn't exist on e.g. `GET /indexes/{indexUid}` (An index having an invalid uid will never exist) and this is, I believe, common to most APIs. 

This 404 behavior is also extended when requesting to update a resource that does not exist. `POST - /indexes/{indexUid}/documents`. In my opinion, the fact that the index is created asynchronously in this case (if it does not exist yet) should not override the `404` with another error since the primary goal of this resource is not creating an index at first.

What do you think?

Ps: Thanks for the private key 🏴‍☠️

Checked with @gmourier and the @meilisearch/core-team, need to change [the spec (API key)](https://github.com/meilisearch/specifications/blob/main/text/0085-api-keys.md) before starting this issue

We should write an error should be sent if the index format is not correct

I've updated the spec here: https://github.com/meilisearch/specifications/pull/113/files

> Sending a value that is not a valid `index` (e.g. regarding the index uid format) in the `indexes` field returns an [invalid_api_key_indexes](0061-error-format-and-definitions.md#invalid_api_key_indexes) with a variant error message. See "Sending an invalid index uid format in `indexes` field" variant.

Definitely something that can be fixed by an external contributor! Feel free to ask for help
